To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TTC12 is the gene mutated in four independent PCD families with a peculiar phenotype characterized by the loss of ODAs and single-headed IDAs in spermatozoa, whereas cilia are normal.

TTC12 mutations result in a PCD phenotype with a unique IDA defect restricted only to a subset of IDAs that are present in cilia and absent in flagella, thus uncovering a new dynein assembly mechanism in cilia versus flagellum.

we have identified TTC12, a cytoplasmatic protein, as a gene involved with the primary ciliary dyskenesia (PCD) disease, a disease characterized by respiratory infections and male infertility, in which cilia and flagellar movement is impaired.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underpin human motile ciliogenesis, with a particular focus on the identification of the proteins involved in ciliary and flagellar dynein assembly.
the identification of genes responsible for primary ciliary dyskenesis, an autosomal recessive genetic disease that affects motile cilia.
understanding the mechanisms that control cilia and flagellum motility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TTC12 is required for the assembly of a subset of IDAs that are present only in flagella, but not in cilia.

TTC12 is a gene involved in primary ciliary disease, which causes a peculiar phenotype characterized by the presence of IDAs in cilia, but not in flagella, and by the absence of a subset of IDAs that are restricted to flagella.
TTC12 is involved in the biogenesis of IDAs, and this process is distinct in cilia and flagellar axonemes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TTC12 is a novel PCD-associated gene that is involved in the assembly of a subset of IDAs in cilia and flagellar axonemes.

we have identified a gene that is required for the assembly of the inner dynein arms (IDA) in cilia and flagellum, but that is only required for the assembly in the flagellum of one particular type of IDA, the so-called single-headed IDA.

the TTC12 gene encodes a cytosolic protein that is required for the assembly of the IDA in ciliated epithelia, and that the absence of TTC12 in sperm leads to the absence of the IDA, whereas the IDA is only partially absent in cilia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanisms of ciliary and flagellar assembly are different.
the assembly of the outer and inner axonemal dynein arm (ODA and IDA) complexes, respectively, is regulated differently in motile cilia (MC) and flagella (FL).
we identify a new gene TTC12, involved in the assembly of the outer dynein arm in motile cilia and flagellum.
